questions.topic: External Merge Sort: Runs, Merging, and Memory Limits
questions.question: What is a sorted run in external merge sort?
options: A memory-sized block sorted in RAM and written as an immutable run
A random collection of records appended to one shared storage page
A hash bucket holding every record that shares the same final key
A complete output file produced before any input record has been read

questions.topic: External Merge Sort: Runs, Merging, and Memory Limits
questions.question: Why does external merge sort favor sequential I/O?
options: Sequential reads make comparison sorting asymptotically constant time
Large sequential transfers amortize latency and avoid scattered storage access
Sequential writes allow records to remain globally unsorted after merging
Object stores require every record to be fetched as a separate random request

questions.topic: External Merge Sort: Runs, Merging, and Memory Limits
questions.question: A 1 TB input is sorted with 8 GB of usable run memory. About how many initial runs result?

questions.topic: External Merge Sort: Runs, Merging, and Memory Limits
questions.question: Why might increasing merge fan-in eventually hurt throughput?
options: Higher fan-in always adds one more complete merge level to the job
Higher fan-in leaves each initial run only partially sorted on disk
Higher fan-in removes the need for separate input and output buffers
Higher fan-in shrinks every buffer and can exhaust descriptor limits

questions.topic: External Merge Sort: Runs, Merging, and Memory Limits
questions.question: Why should run files be named deterministically and committed only after complete writes?
options: A retry can reuse verified runs without exposing partial artifacts
A retry can append duplicate records to every incomplete run
A reader can consume a run while its sort order is still changing
A merge can omit checksums because names prove record correctness

questions.topic: External Merge Sort: Runs, Merging, and Memory Limits
questions.question: Why is sizing runs from raw record payload alone unsafe?
options: Raw payload already includes every runtime and temporary allocation twice
Sorting, offsets, decoding, and the runtime require additional memory headroom
External sorting cannot spill until all input fits in physical memory
Operating-system caching eliminates memory use by sort implementations

questions.question: What does the heap hold during a K-way merge?
options: Every unconsumed record from every run
Only the final record from the largest run
At most the current head record from each run
One random record selected independently from each run

questions.question: What is the time complexity of heap-based merging for N total records across K runs?
options: O(N)
O(K log N)
O(NK)
O(N log K)

questions.question: After emitting the smallest heap entry, which input record is read next?
options: The next record from the same run as the emitted entry
The next record from every run before rebuilding the heap
The median record from the run with the largest remaining size
The first record of a newly generated unsorted run

questions.question: Why should heap entries include a stable secondary key such as run ID?
options: It reduces the number of runs to one before merging starts
It defines deterministic order when primary keys compare equal
It changes the heap from a min-heap into a max-heap
It guarantees that duplicate records are always removed

questions.question: Why can multi-level merging outperform one enormous fan-in on real hardware?
options: It converts every run into an unsorted hash partition before merging
It avoids reading and writing the dataset at any merge level at all
It keeps buffers and stream counts practical for one extra I/O pass
It lowers the required output size below the number of input records

questions.question: How should a merged object be published on object storage?
options: Mutate the public object in place while readers are consuming it
Append one byte per heap comparison to the existing public object
Expose the destination name before its first run head has been read
Write a temporary object, validate it, then publish a manifest

questions.topic: Why Index Construction Is a Sorting Problem
questions.question: Which tuple order directly supports inverted-index construction?
options: (term, document ID, position)
(worker ID, arrival time, random value)
(position, hash bucket, document length)
(document title, file size, process ID)

questions.topic: Why Index Construction Is a Sorting Problem
questions.question: What becomes possible when equal terms are adjacent in the sorted stream?
options: The builder can skip tokenization and invent the missing positions
The builder can group occurrences into one sequential postings list
The builder must randomly update every prior document in the corpus
The builder can drop document IDs because term order implies them

questions.topic: Why Index Construction Is a Sorting Problem
questions.question: Documents produce term occurrences in document order. Why is sorting required?
options: The final index must retain only original document processing order
Tokenization cannot produce a term or document identifier
The index must regroup occurrences by term and ordered document ID
The index requires every term to remain separated from equal terms

questions.topic: Why Index Construction Is a Sorting Problem
questions.question: Why is a giant in-memory term-to-postings map insufficient at corpus scale?
options: A map cannot associate one term with more than a single document
A map always writes its postings as sorted immutable runs by itself
A map guarantees vocabulary and postings stay smaller than free RAM
A map's vocabulary, buffers, and object overhead can outgrow RAM

questions.topic: Why Index Construction Is a Sorting Problem
questions.question: How do immutable segments make dynamic indexing practical?
options: Build sorted segments for updates and merge them in the background
Resort the entire corpus synchronously after every new document
Insert every occurrence randomly into one immutable postings file
Keep unlimited segments forever without any query or merge cost

questions.topic: Why Index Construction Is a Sorting Problem
questions.question: Why does sorting by document ID and position also improve postings compression?
options: It makes consecutive values larger and requires fixed-width storage
It creates small positive gaps that need fewer encoded bits
It duplicates term strings for every occurrence in the output
It removes the ability to distinguish positions within a document
